key_insight: PosteriorBench argues that evaluating generative inverse solvers by only point estimates is misleading: a method must match the full posterior distribution, not just produce one plausible answer. The benchmark shifts attention from "looks right" reconstructions to whether uncertainty, multimodality, and mode coverage are faithfully captured.
problem_solved: Current evaluation methods for generative inverse problems often reward a single high-quality reconstruction even when the true solution is ambiguous. This paper addresses the gap between pointwise accuracy and posterior fidelity in ill-posed scientific inverse tasks.
method: Introduces PosteriorBench, a benchmark focused on posterior matching rather than single-sample reconstruction quality.
Evaluates generative inverse solvers on their ability to represent uncertainty, preserve multiple modes, and avoid overconfident or collapsed outputs.
Compares methods using posterior-aware criteria to expose failures hidden by traditional point-estimate metrics.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more realistic way to judge inverse solvers in scientific settings where many answers may be valid. It encourages building models that are not only accurate, but also calibrated and uncertainty-aware.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of point estimate evaluation vs posterior matching
Diagram of an ill-posed inverse problem showing multiple valid reconstructions from the same observation
Posterior density plots illustrating mode collapse vs true multimodal distribution
Benchmark scorecard with metrics for accuracy, uncertainty, and mode coverage
paper_title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
paper_authors: Jiachen Yao, Zi-Siang Hsu, Xi Deng, Aditi Gupta, Xin Ju
